121: Thank you for the feedback from parents and kids – hopefully we'll manage to organise another edition.
124: We have some footage from elektrobikefestival.cz, or rather from its partly rained-out Saturday.
126: We are honoured that from 3 to 5 July we will be looking after young riders at the {1}{2}MTB Trilogy{3}{4} stage race as part of our new project {5}{6}Bikeskills.cz{7}{8}. If you are interested in technique coaching, don't hesitate to contact the event organisers directly. Of course this also applies to those who want to have fun in Enduro, XC and other disciplines.
127: You'll find more information on their website {1}{2}MTB Trilogy …{3}{4}
128: 27–28/5 – Bikeskills camps and an exhibition at the spa
129: Saturday for female bikers and Sunday for male bikers. Beautiful weather and enthusiasm for coaching gave Katarína Tóthová on Saturday, and Vlasta with Mára Tryner on Sunday, the ideal weapon for pushing the limits of the riders who came. On Saturday the women rode literally flat out and apparently even flew over the handlebars (luckily without injury). On Sunday we also rode harder trails, and hopefully both the Enduro and XC guys were happy. Everyone rode their own lines, as far as their head and bike allowed.
130: For Lukáš Valný and Vlasta, Saturday also included a trip to the beautiful surroundings of the Jáchymov spa, where the springs were being christened. A rich programme, crowds of spectators and great weather. The organisers won the lottery, and although we couldn't use our full obstacle setup because of space, we gave it everything to make the spectators' day better. Martin Šimůnek also rode a few Moravian exhibitions, including the felling of the maypole in Rouské, and workshops.
131: Motorbike blessing and Jílové near Děčín
132: {1}7/5 – Exhibition and workshop in Jílové near Děčín – Motorbike blessing{2}
133: Martin Šimůnek and Lukáš Valný set off to Jílové near Děčín for the annual motorbike blessing. Their job wasn't just to jump for crowds of kids and adult spectators, but also to run our workshop, where everyone could test how good they are at riding over obstacles and their technique. Martin once again showed his quality as a host – and that he matures like wine with age. The organisers' thanks are always nice, and thank you for the invitation.
135: Horní Maršov was dominated by two experienced riders: Petr Jeřicha, who focuses mainly on Enduro due to a back injury, but whose Trial title still shows. Together with Michal Budský, who rides a street bike, they alone would probably have been enough for the organisers – but why not show the young ones how riders their own age ride? Matouš Balík is a new member of our team and a young gun in the club at junior level. Despite being in the middle of his school-leaving exams, he went with Petr and Michal to gain experience and ride with legends of the Trial sport. Here too we received positive feedback from the organisers, and we thank them for the invitation and the great atmosphere.
136: Reports from exhibitions and workshops over the last two weekends
138: A small village in the north held a cycling day, and our team – Lukáš Valný, Vlasta Kabeláč Čiháček and kids from the club – was invited too. Unfortunately the weather was a bit harsher, and the temperature with the possibility of a storm didn't attract many spectators. Anyway, a few true believers came, so we could show them a bit of Trial riding over obstacles, and after the exhibition Vlasta tried some gaps onto a tree trunk and the local walls in the grounds.
139: {1}31/5 – Triple exhibition – all over the Czech Republic{2}
140: Storms wherever you looked, but a pleasant temperature. We played roulette all over the Czech Republic. Near Jablůnkov, Lukáš Valný and Michal Budský started their exhibition at the edge of a storm cloud, but everything went as it should. Martin Šimůnek took his workshop to Moravia, where he managed to ride part of the programme before the rest was unfortunately washed out. And the biggest group – Vlasta Kabeláč Čiháček and the kids, Marek Tryner as host and Tobík Dolák as workshop instructor – headed to Most. Unfortunately, due to a knee injury, Mára is having ligament surgery in a few days, and Tobík Dolák overdid his training enthusiasm and found out what it's like to land on your tailbone from height. So the riding was on Vlasta and the kids, followed by a workshop on Trial bikes and obstacles. Luckily the weather turned out ideal, so mission accomplished on all fronts.
142: Village festival exhibition in Dolní Řasnice
143: A demanding first exhibition after injury for Vlasta, and also for the other riders, who had to cope with the extreme heat at the event in picturesque Řasnice. We were a bit surprised by an almost hour-long traffic jam on the way to Liberec, which delayed other performers at the event too.
144: The locals were already in full swing when we arrived, and the mayor welcomed us in full gear. On the gravel surface we had a carpet ready to ride on. Lukáš Valný, Vlasta and young guns Márty, Elli and Nikol launched into the exhibition, which entertained the spectators hiding in the tent, and several of them didn't mind playing living obstacles in the sun.
145: Thanks for the invitation and the encouragement.
147: This weekend we ran the last Bikeskills weekend camps. Both the women's and men's camps brought together a decent group of riders who wanted to improve and progress – each within their own abilities, of course.
148: After the morning basics, pump track, berms and – for the men – jumps, we moved to the nearby Marvánek swimming pool for lunch and then along our traditional route, where we have various technical spots ready, from drops and Trial to descents for riders of all levels.
149: Many thanks to all participants for their effort, their patience with our explanations and the appreciation at the end. Hopefully Vlasta, Katarína and Matouš passed something on to you.
153: The traditional event organised by the MTB & Trial Mraveniště Říčany club under the leadership of Vlasta Kabeláč Čiháček has grown somewhat since Pavel Hájek (former manager of the FORBIKES trade fair) joined.
154: The traditional event organised by the MTB & Trial Mraveniště Říčany club under the leadership of Vlasta Kabeláč Čiháček has grown somewhat since Pavel Hájek (former manager of the FORBIKES trade fair) joined. This year the programme was expanded, the event returned to a two-day format (as in the days of hosting international UCI C1 races) and an Expo zone was added.
155: Big plans, demanding preparation – but the fate of outdoor events is always the roulette called weather. Šlapačky really got a taste of it this year. On the Monday before the race a storm arrived that completely destroyed the Tehov pump track. Thanks to the municipality of Tehov and Michal Maroši, a group of people was found who restored it almost to its original state, which – had it lasted – would have guaranteed a beautifully groomed track. Unfortunately, on Friday evening and practically all of Saturday all hell broke loose in Říčany and Tehov. The rain only stopped late on Saturday afternoon. The pump track was again practically half destroyed. But every event organiser knows you have to fight for success. So repairs to the pump track went on late into the night, with the promised warmer, sunny Sunday in prospect. Fortunately, it came.
156: Practically most of Saturday's disciplines were moved to Sunday in a limited form. First to start was the rescheduled kids' Trial race, where spectators could admire the art of overcoming obstacles performed by the youngest kids from the club and guests. The race was ridden under modified rules that motivate riders to complete the whole section more than the current official rules do.
157: Because of the schedule the race was run quickly, and some riders could jump straight into the kids' MTB XC races, which were very physically demanding as the terrain slowly dried out. Parents cheered and the kids didn't give away a centimetre. The difficulty was reflected in the number of riders who gave up in the high humidity and heat – but hats off to them for finding the courage to race in these conditions.
158: Next came the adults' Trial exhibition race, which was something of a Trial celebration. Four generations of Trial riders faced each other in one race. Vlasta Kabeláč Čiháček, 10-time Czech Elite champion, against his master, multiple world champion Martin Šimůnek, who after almost 10 years of riding exhibitions tried racing again. As if that weren't enough, local native, Czech champion and Vlasta's student Petr Jeřicha also returned after 5 years. The circle was completed by Matouš Balík, Lukáš Valný and other guys from the club. Victory across all course difficulties went to Petr Jeřicha ahead of Martin and Vlasta. The latter took the win in the Elite category and the Trial record. The bunny hop contest was won by Lukáš Valný.
159: While the adults' Trial was still going, training started on the pump track, which had dried a little. Pump track training had to be banned all morning. Conditions were the same for all riders, and although the track was slow and physically demanding, there were lots of great performances in the battles for fat prize money, trophies and medals.
160: This year more than 115 riders started at the event, lots of fans came, and even more were unfortunately put off by the weather. You'll be able to watch footage from the event on ČT Déčko, or on the Trialshow and Bikeskills team YouTube channels once the edit is finished.
161: We look forward to seeing you at next year's edition – hopefully the weather order will work out this time..
162: The men at camp enjoyed both rain and sunshine
163: This year's first camp for men was very much about May drizzle. The forecast was completely off – when it was supposed to be sunny it rained, and vice versa. Anyway, it wasn't a downpour, and a classic windbreaker kept everyone alive and at a reasonable operating temperature.
164: As it was an intermediate camp, it was clear we'd tackle harder things. After the morning classics in the Tehov park we went straight to the descents in the former quarry, where a few tricky muddy, rocky lines run. In the end everyone found their limit, and more than one die-hard who couldn't resist temptation ended up on their side on the slope. Fortunately there were no serious injuries or trips to hospital, and in the end everyone outdid themselves and hopefully took away something useful from the camp for the trails and the future..
165: Now just repeat, train and try :) Hopefully see you again at a men's camp during/after the summer holidays.
167: A traditional exhibition date is European Car-Free Day, when our team is fully booked. This year the fastest to book were the organisers in Štětí and in Prague. Lukáš Valný, Marek Tryner and, somewhat unplanned, Matouš Balík rode together at Náměstí Republiky in Prague, enjoying a beautiful sunny day.
168: Vlasta and Martin Šimůnek, on the other hand, had slightly gloomy weather, but still pleasant riding on the square in Štětí, where kids from local schools came along.
169: Both events were also workshops where kids could borrow Trial and regular MTB bikes to try out.
170: Ball of the association of municipalities in Čepřovice
171: We received an invitation from Čepřovice near Strakonice, where a ball of 6 municipalities was being held. Nothing was left to chance – the organiser booked us back in January, so we were free and the team of Vlasta Kabeláč Čiháček and Lukáš Valný could head to the event. Besides the mayor, we also had kids on hand, who gave us great support. The atmosphere was lively, as is usual at village balls, and from among the sportsmen and sportswomen we chose a few volunteers who weren't afraid to lie down under our bikes. Thanks for the invitation – hopefully see you at an exhibition or workshop next year.
172: Sorry for the lower photo quality – we only managed to get a video, from which they were created.
174: Our farewell to the Tehov park before winter – and hopefully its spring rebuild – in the form of small races and training was moved a bit. There was a risk that few riders would come because of the long weekend, but in the end the turnout was a surprise. About 20 riders started in Trial and a similar number on the pump track, which is about half of the club's members. The weather was for tougher characters – alternately muddy, but without rain – but the kids didn't mind and the adult riders survived too 🙂
175: As every year, the rules were based on OPEN FREE, with riders choosing the arrows they want to ride and the difficulty. Categories were divided by age and, for older riders, by riders. Each rider had to adapt the course to themselves with a limit of 5–6 arrows per section. Riding was in groups, each with its own judge, who could also adjust the rules to suit the riders.
176: It was great that a few club legends who don't normally come to training showed up too. Michal Havránek got up from his director's chair, saddled his blue Ozonys and battled more with his physical fitness – which, as he said, he needs to catch up on – than with the bike. Martin Šimůnek rode his last big event on a 24” before switching to 26”, on which he won a number of world titles, and he really surprised in his duel with Míra Brunclík. Honestly, doing gaps onto around 10–11 pallets in the mud after turning 50 is insane, and on one of the sections in the first round Míra and Martin even managed to beat Mára and Vlasta. At the other end of the age spectrum, a Martin also cleverly took 3rd place – but this one from the Gomboš family.
